items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSD: stop registering with rpcbind after a failure in listener_set

nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() calls svc_xprt_create_from_sa() once for each
requested listener and passes flags of 0, so every listener registers with
rpcbind on its own. A rpcbind that accepts the connection and never replies
therefore costs one timeout for each entry. With the cap of 1024 entries
the request can hold nfsd_mutex for about 34 minutes, which is roughly 17
times the hung-task threshold.

One failure is enough to know that the next call will not fare better.
Read svc_rpcb_failure_count() before the create loop, and pass
SVC_SOCK_ANONYMOUS for the rest of the request once the count moves.
items.title: NFSD: stop registering with rpcbind after a failure in listener_set

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/9p/usbg: also disable endpoints on p9_usbg_close

The close function has to fully reverse the state change of 9p_create
(mount) and the potential call of set_alt(1). This includes to ensure
that the usage of the endpoints is not active any more.
items.title: net/9p/usbg: also disable endpoints on p9_usbg_close

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/9p/usbg: set client to Disconnected on usb9pfs_disable

This patch is setting the client status to Disconnected, when the
client is still in use. Otherwise a disconnected usb cable would run
any use of the mount to faults.
items.title: net/9p/usbg: set client to Disconnected on usb9pfs_disable

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/drm_crtc: ensure dma_fence_ops remain valid during device unbind

In [1], sashiko reported the following issue:

=== snip ===
Looking at how these fences are managed, drm_crtc_create_fence()
creates a dma_fence without taking a reference to the drm_device or
drm_crtc. Because the sync_file framework exposes this fence to
userspace, the fence can outlive the CRTC.

The dma_fence contract requires that data accessed by dma_fence_ops
(like get_driver_name) must remain valid for an RCU grace period after
the fence is signaled. However, drm_crtc_cleanup() and the subsequent
freeing of the device do not wait for an RCU grace period via
synchronize_rcu().

If userspace calls ioctl(SYNC_IOC_FILE_INFO) concurrently with a device
hot-unplug:

CPU1 (Userspace)
sync_file_get_name()
  ops = rcu_dereference(fence->ops);
  if (!dma_fence_test_signaled_flag())
    // Preempted or delayed here

CPU2 (Driver Teardown)
Signals the fence (setting fence->ops = NULL)
Destroys and frees the CRTC without waiting for an RCU grace period

CPU1 (Resumes)
  ops->get_driver_name(fence) -> drm_crtc_fence_get_driver_name()
  crtc = fence_to_crtc(fence); // Casts to the freed CRTC
  return crtc->dev->driver->name; // Use-after-free

...

Does the CRTC or DRM device need to be kept alive for the RCU grace
period, or should the fence hold a proper reference to prevent the
use-after-free when get_driver_name() and get_timeline_name() access
the freed CRTC structure?
=== snap ===

I believe this to be a correct observation and this patch implements
the suggestion of waiting for an RCU grace period before proceeding
with destruction of the drm_crtc, so that get_driver_name() and
get_timeline_name() can still work.
items.title: drm/drm_crtc: ensure dma_fence_ops remain valid during device unbind

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: target: Fix demo-mode dynamic ACL dev-entry UAF vs LUN teardown

A demo-mode (generate_node_acls=1) login that allocates a dynamic NodeACL
populates that ACL's per-LUN dev entries in core_tpg_add_node_to_devs()
*before* the ACL is linked onto tpg->acl_node_list by
target_add_node_acl():

	core_tpg_check_initiator_node_acl():
		...
		core_tpg_add_node_to_devs(acl, tpg, NULL); /* builds deves */
		target_add_node_acl(acl);                  /* only now listed */

The LUN teardown sweep, core_clear_lun_from_tpg(), enumerates only
tpg->acl_node_list, so a dev entry whose ACL is still in the window above
is invisible to the sweep and is never disabled.  It is left on the
se_lun->lun_deve_list after core_tpg_remove_lun() frees the se_lun; when
the same unpacked_lun is later re-added and the se_lun is reallocated at
the same address, the stale dev entry is rediscovered by
target_nacl_find_deve() and core_enable_device_list_for_node() corrupts
lun_deve_list:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free ...
   core_enable_device_list_for_node+0x5ce/0x880
   core_tpg_add_node_to_devs+0x169/0x190
   core_dev_add_lun+0x146/0x190
   target_fabric_port_link+0xe9/0x1b0
   configfs_symlink+0x381/0xae0
   __x64_sys_symlink+0x55/0x80

The demo-mode login path that drives the ACL/dev-entry creation is
reachable by an unauthenticated initiator; the colliding LUN add/remove is
a local configfs operation.

Commit 49cb77e297dc ("target: Avoid mappedlun symlink creation during lun
shutdown") introduced se_lun->lun_shutdown and guarded the *explicit* ACL
MappedLUN path (target_fabric_mappedlun_link()), but the demo-mode
automatic path, core_tpg_add_node_to_devs() ->
core_enable_device_list_for_node(), was never given the equivalent guard,
and the publish-after-populate ordering in
core_tpg_check_initiator_node_acl() was left unchanged.

Fix it in three cooperating parts:

 1) Publish the dynamic NodeACL onto acl_node_list *before* creating its
    dev entries, so the teardown sweep can observe them.

 2) Refuse to attach a dev entry to an se_lun that is shutting down,
    checked under nacl->lun_entry_mutex -- the same lock the sweep takes --
    so once the sweep has passed an ACL any later enable for that LUN
    observes lun_shutdown and skips it.

 3) In core_enable_device_list_for_node(), insert the new dev entry onto
    lun->lun_deve_list while still holding nacl->lun_entry_mutex, in both
    the replace and the new-entry branch.  Previously the entry was added
    to nacl->lun_entry_hlist under the mutex but to lun->lun_deve_list only
    after dropping it; with the ACL now published early, the sweep could
    take the mutex in that gap, find the entry on the hlist,
    core_disable_device_list_for_node() it (list_del() on the not-yet-
    linked lun_link succeeds and the entry is freed), and then the enable
    would list_add_tail() the freed entry back onto lun_deve_list.  Linking
    both lists under the mutex makes enable and the sweep mutually
    exclusive, closing that window.

core_tpg_add_node_to_devs() already ignores the return value of
core_enable_device_list_for_node(), so a shutting-down LUN is simply
skipped.
items.title: scsi: target: Fix demo-mode dynamic ACL dev-entry UAF vs LUN teardown

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

batman-adv: tt: don't drop local events queued during TVLV update

batadv_tt_tvlv_container_update() read the number of local changes without
holding changes_list_lock. batadv_tt_local_event() is not serialized by
the commit_lock and can queue new events before the changes_list is
flushed:

  CPU0                          CPU1
  batadv_tt_tvlv_container_update()
    num = ...local_changes;
                                batadv_tt_local_event()
                                  list_add_tail(...);
                                  ...local_changes++;
    spin_lock_bh(&...changes_list_lock);
    /* only num events copied but all freed */

The additional events were freed without ever being sent. Other nodes will
only notice this via a CRC mismatch and must request the full table.

The number of changes and the changes_list must therefore be taken
atomically. Events queued afterwards then stay in the tt.changes_list for
the next TT round.

The changes can no longer be kept for the next round when the TVLV buffer
allocation fails. But they would be sent with a skipped TTVN anyway, so the
other nodes have to request the full table in this case either way. The
last changeset is only dropped in this case when the TTVN was incremented.
Without new changes, it still describes the current TTVN.

Previously, the unconsumed changes caused a retry of the TVLV container
update in the next commit round. Since the changes are now consumed, the
next round would only take the path without changes and wait for
BATADV_TT_OGM_APPEND_MAX rounds before updating the container again. Until
then, the outdated container with the previous TTVN would still be
announced. The ogm_append_cnt is therefore reset on failure to retry the
update in the next OGM interval.

This doesn't make the CRC consistent with the announced changeset. The
local table modifications are still not serialized with the commit and
batadv_tt_local_transition_new() can still make a client part of the CRC
for which the event is only part of the next TT round. Such an
inconsistency is detected by the CRC check of the other nodes and solved
via a full table request.
items.title: batman-adv: tt: don't drop local events queued during TVLV update

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sctp: account for chunk padding in sctp_init_cause()

sctp_init_cause() accepts a chunk when skb_tailroom() can hold the
cause header and the payload. sctp_addto_chunk() then writes 0-3
bytes of padding before that header so the chunk stays 4-byte
aligned. The check does not include the padding, and the following
skb_put() calls skb_over_panic() from softirq.

Count the padding sctp_addto_chunk() is about to write. The cause
length on the wire stays the header plus the payload.

Found by LLM inspection, triggered and tested the fix.
items.title: sctp: account for chunk padding in sctp_init_cause()

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

btrfs: sysfs: restore NOFS context on early return in btrfs_sysfs_add_block_group_type()

btrfs_sysfs_add_block_group_type() sets up a NOFS context with
memalloc_nofs_save() because kobject_add() performs GFP_KERNEL
allocations deep in its call chain, and the function may be called
while holding a transaction handle or a lock required for a
transaction commit, where reclaim could deadlock.

Every other return path of this function calls memalloc_nofs_restore()
except the early return taken when another thread has already created
the kobject for the same raid index (this can happen when restriping).
Taking that path leaves PF_MEMALLOC_NOFS set on the calling task, so
all subsequent memory allocations performed by that task remain
restricted to the NOFS scope, which may lead to unexpected allocation
failures or deadlocks later on.

Restore the NOFS context before returning from that path.
items.title: btrfs: sysfs: restore NOFS context on early return in btrfs_sysfs_add_block_group_type()

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

btrfs: prevent deleting the wrong subvolume by ID

When deleting a subvolume by ID, btrfs_ioctl_snap_destroy() first
resolves the requested ID to a name, then looks up that name again
under the parent directory lock.

A concurrent rename can change which subvolume is associated with
the name between these operations. Since the deletion path does not
verify the ID of the resolved subvolume, it can delete a different
subvolume while leaving the requested one intact.

This was reproduced by repeatedly exchanging the names of two
subvolumes using renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE) while deleting one of
them by ID. The wrong subvolume was deleted in 9 out of 14 independent
tests.

Fix this by checking that the resolved subvolume ID matches the
requested ID while holding the parent directory lock. Return -EAGAIN
on a mismatch so that userspace can retry the operation instead of
being told that the requested subvolume does not exist.
items.title: btrfs: prevent deleting the wrong subvolume by ID

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/shmem: stop retrying folios that cannot be split

A fault or collapse can insert a large folio crossing EOF after
shmem_undo_range() has handled the boundary folios. If splitting that
folio fails, truncate_inode_partial_folio() retains it when it is dirty.
The final scan then repeatedly finds it because it restarts from an
unchanged start.

Truncation keeps the inode lock and ignores fatal signals while looping.
A concurrent unlink() can then block other directory operations while
holding the directory lock and waiting for the file's lock.

Advance start past the retained folio, whose truncated part has already
been zeroed. Do not move start backwards if the failed split has shrunk
the folio.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: split fixes, simplify descriptions, adjust comments ]
items.title: mm/shmem: stop retrying folios that cannot be split

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/shmem: fix truncate hang in large swap entry

Truncating a tmpfs file or memfd to a page-aligned size inside a large
swap entry can loop indefinitely in shmem_undo_range(). The task holds
the inode lock and cannot be killed.

A large swap entry represents a whole swapped-out folio. For example,
truncate a file whose pages 0-7 share one swap entry to four pages:

    [ 0  1  2  3 | 4  5  6  7 ]
         keep    |   discard
                 ^
            new EOF, start = 4

i_size has already been updated when boundary handling asks
shmem_get_partial_folio() for page 4. Since it is swapped out, the helper
calls shmem_get_folio() with SGP_READ. That rejects page 4 with -EINVAL
because its starting offset equals i_size. Nothing is read back.

The final scan cannot free the entry without losing pages 0-3. It skips
it, restarts from start = 4, and finds it again indefinitely. An unaligned
truncate avoids this particular failure because the requested page starts
below i_size. Folios already in the page-cache cannot trigger it as the
direct lookup will return them beyond EOF.

Fix it by letting shmem_get_partial_folio() call shmem_swapin_folio()
directly for swap entries. This bypasses the read path's i_size check,
allowing the existing boundary handling to zero and split the folio. If
swap-in returns a smaller folio, it also splits the swap entry so the
final scan can free the entries beyond EOF. Retry the lookup if the entry
changes during swap-in.

Handling swap-in allocation failures remains broken and is unchanged by
this commit. Even when shmem_swapin_folio() correctly returns -ENOMEM
instead of -EEXIST, shmem_get_partial_folio() returns NULL and
shmem_undo_range() skips boundary handling. If the large swap entry
remains intact, truncation can still loop in the final scan, while hole
punching can return without zeroing the boundary.

This may read an entire large folio back from swap while holding
i_rwsem, only to discard part of it. Avoiding that I/O would require
splitting both the swap entry and any large folio still in the swap
cache. That, however, is much bigger work.
items.title: mm/shmem: fix truncate hang in large swap entry

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/shmem: fix truncate loop after boundary swapin failure

If swapping in a large entry at the new EOF fails, shmem_undo_range()
leaves the entry in place. Its final scan skips the entry, then restarts
from the same start index and finds it again. Truncation can loop forever
while holding i_rwsem.

Advance start past the skipped entry so that a restarted scan can finish,
as we already do for folios that cannot be split.

Note that this does not fix the missing zeroing when boundary swapin fails,
it merely prevents the endless loop.
items.title: mm/shmem: fix truncate loop after boundary swapin failure

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/filemap: read mapping->a_ops->free_folio under i_lock

memory_failure() -> ... -> filemap_remove_folio() can read mapping->a_ops
after the inode has been freed. Once the folio is deleted from the
pagecache it no longer pins the mapping, so after i_lock is dropped
e.g., a concurrent final iput() can evict and free the inode before
filemap_free_folio() looks up mapping->a_ops->free_folio.

Most callers hold a reference on the inode, but not all.

Documentation/filesystems/vfs.rst explicitly states that ->free_folio()
must not assume the original address_space mapping still exists.

Fix it by loading ->free_folio while i_lock is still held, similar to
what folio_unmap_invalidate() does.

Inline filemap_free_folio() into its remaining caller such that
delete_from_page_cache_batch() also just loads the callback before
dropping the i_lock.

The bug was found by code inspection and has not been reproduced.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

[ david: get rid of filemap_free_folio() entirely; improve patch description ]
items.title: mm/filemap: read mapping->a_ops->free_folio under i_lock

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/filemap: finish fault cleanup before dropping the fault lock

On a retried fault, a fatal signal interrupting the folio lock wait
makes lock_folio_maybe_drop_mmap() drop the fault lock without pinning
the file. However, filemap_fault() may still need to release
mapping->invalidate_lock. A concurrent munmap() can release the last
file reference and free the mapping before that unlock.

Defer dropping the fault lock to filemap_fault()'s retry cleanup, after
releasing invalidate_lock. If the fault lock was already dropped for
I/O, release the existing file reference instead. Keep the fault lock
held for FAULT_FLAG_RETRY_NOWAIT as before.
items.title: mm/filemap: finish fault cleanup before dropping the fault lock

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/rmap: handle device-exclusive entries in folio_referenced_one()

page_vma_mapped_walk() can return non-present device-exclusive entries,
but folio_referenced_one() passes them to PTE young-bit accessors that
require present PTEs.

We must neither call clear_flush_young_ptes_notify() nor
folio_pte_batch() with non-present entries. For example, clearing the
young bit on non-present PTEs can corrupt the entry: on arm64
PTE_AF overlaps the swap type, so clearing it turns a device-exclusive
entry into an ordinary swap entry.

folio_pte_batch() will VM_WARN_ON_FOLIO.

Apply the same approach as the previous fixes to e.g., damon_ptep_mkold():
treat these entries as old from the CPU's perspective and obtain their
young state through the MMU notifier.

Skip PTE batching and MGLRU look-around for non-present entries, and
don't modify non-present PTEs.
items.title: mm/rmap: handle device-exclusive entries in folio_referenced_one()

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/huge_memory: fix list corruption when deferred_split_scan() races with deferred_split_folio()

Since the deferred split queue became a list_lru, the isolate callback
moves the folios it took a reference on to an on-stack list, linked
through folio->_deferred_list, and deferred_split_scan() takes them off
that list with list_del_init() without holding the list_lru lock.

deferred_split_folio() does not know about the on-stack list. It only
holds the list_lru lock when it looks at the same list_head, and it can
run for such a folio: a THP is queued when it is mapped, as a candidate
for the underused check, and is queued "again" when a part of it gets
unmapped:

  CPU0 deferred_split_scan()          CPU1 deferred_split_folio()
  list_del_init(&folio->_deferred_list)
    next->prev = prev
    prev->next = next
    entry->next = entry
                                      list_lru_lock_irqsave()
                                      folio_set_partially_mapped()
                                      __list_lru_add()
                                        list_empty(item)  -> true
                                        list_add_tail(item, &l->list)
                                          item->next = &l->list
                                          item->prev = tail
    entry->prev = entry

The folio now sits on the list_lru with ->prev pointing to itself. The
next removal leaves the neighbours pointing to it, and they still do so
after the folio has been freed. With CONFIG_DEBUG_LIST:

  list_del corruption. prev->next should be ffd4000000270090, but was
  ffd4000000278090. (prev=ffd4000000270090)

Fix it by grabbing the lock around list_del_init() so
deferred_split_folio() cannot race with it.
items.title: mm/huge_memory: fix list corruption when deferred_split_scan() races with deferred_split_folio()

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/huge_memory: properly handle refcounted PUD mappings on fork

copy_huge_pud() copies device-DAX entries without taking a folio reference
or updating mapcounts and the child's RSS.

For example, MADV_GUARD_INSTALL sets VM_MAYBE_GUARD on a device-DAX VMA,
forcing copy_page_range() to traverse the whole VMA on fork. Any remaining
huge PUDs are then copied without accounting for the new mappings.
Unmapping them in the child decrements accounting that was never added.

Use vm_normal_page_pud() to identify refcounted mappings. Take a folio
reference and add the child's PUD rmap and RSS accounting before installing
the copied entry. Pass src and dst VMAs consistently instead of src and
dst MM. Move the TODO.
items.title: mm/huge_memory: properly handle refcounted PUD mappings on fork

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

cipso: fix optlen corruption in cipso_v4_delopt()

cipso_v4_delopt() recomputes the option length by walking the option
buffer after the CIPSO option has been moved out.  The walk then reads
the stale bytes at the tail of the buffer as option data, and a crafted
setsockopt(IP_OPTIONS) buffer can make it treat one of them as an option
length, increasing opt->opt.optlen beyond the valid option data.

The corrupted length stays on the socket and is later used as the copy
length by getsockopt(IP_OPTIONS) and by the udp/raw/ping sendmsg paths,
where it exceeds the size of the buffers they copy into.

Compute the new length from the intact options before the move and
subtract the CIPSO length, and fill the padding with IPOPT_END.
items.title: cipso: fix optlen corruption in cipso_v4_delopt()

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ntfs: don't allow compression on volumes with clusters larger than 4K

On a volume made with "mkntfs -c 8192", a user can set
FILE_ATTR_COMPRESSED on an empty file through system.ntfs_attrib.
Writing to the file and reading it back after dropping the page cache
then crashes:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in ntfs_read_compressed_block+0xa2c/0x2040
  Read of size 8192 at addr ffff88804355a000 by task dd/106

The read path only handles clusters up to 4K. It copies each cluster
out of a single page, and a compression block of 16 8K clusters does
not fit in the 64K ntfs_compression_buffer. Loading an inode already
rejects compressed data on such volumes.

Reject the flag change the same way.
items.title: ntfs: don't allow compression on volumes with clusters larger than 4K

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vhost-vdpa: fix pinned page leak in vhost_vdpa_pa_map() error path

When pin_user_pages() or vhost_vdpa_map() fails, vhost_vdpa_pa_map()
is supposed to unpin the pages pinned after the last successfully
mapped chunk, i.e. the range [map_pfn, last_pfn]. The unpin is guarded
by nchunks, but nchunks is reset to 0 every time a chunk is mapped from
inside the current page list, so a failure after any such boundary
leaves that pending range pinned forever. With physically scattered
memory nearly every page list contains a boundary, so the leak happens
on practically every failed IOTLB update.

The pending range is non-empty exactly when a page has been pinned,
which last_pfn already tells us, so drop nchunks and test last_pfn.
items.title: vhost-vdpa: fix pinned page leak in vhost_vdpa_pa_map() error path

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

hwmon: chipcap2: fix IRQ teardown ordering

The threaded IRQs are currently requested before the hwmon device
is registered. Since devres releases resources in reverse order,
the hwmon device is unregistered before the IRQs are freed during
driver teardown. An IRQ may therefore still run after the hwmon
device has been released and access the stale data->hwmon pointer.

Separate IRQ discovery from IRQ registration so that the IRQ numbers
and alarm visibility flags are initialized before registering the
hwmon device while the IRQs are released before the hwmon device
during devres cleanup.
items.title: hwmon: chipcap2: fix IRQ teardown ordering

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

hwmon: (lm87) Fix drvdata type confusion in vrm_show() and vrm_store()

When an LM87 or ADM1024 device is probed with VID support enabled, reading
from or writing to the vrm sysfs attribute triggers a driver data type
confusion in vrm_show() and vrm_store() in drivers/hwmon/lm87.c.

In lm87_probe(), the driver stores the struct lm87_data pointer on the I2C
client via i2c_set_clientdata() and passes the struct i2c_client pointer as
the drvdata argument to devm_hwmon_device_register_with_groups(), which
attaches the attribute groups to the registered hwmon device with client as
its driver_data. Unlike the other sysfs callbacks that retrieve client via
dev_get_drvdata() and then obtain data via i2c_get_clientdata(), vrm_show()
and vrm_store() assign dev_get_drvdata(dev) directly to struct lm87_data *.
Dereferencing data->vrm therefore accesses the struct i2c_client instance
at offsetof(struct lm87_data, vrm), causing vrm_show() to leak an unrelated
byte from struct i2c_client to userspace and vrm_store() to corrupt a byte
within struct i2c_client while failing to update the actual VRM value.

Fix the problem by assigning the return value from dev_get_drvdata(dev) to
struct i2c_client *client and using i2c_get_clientdata() to get the actual
client data.
items.title: hwmon: (lm87) Fix drvdata type confusion in vrm_show() and vrm_store()

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

hwmon: (peci/dimmtemp) Fix devres leak and UAF on concurrent unbind

When a peci_dimmtemp device is unbound concurrently with its delayed
initialization work (detect_work), newly allocated devm resources and
the hwmon device are leaked, leading to a use-after-free when reading
the lingering hwmon sysfs attributes.

In peci_dimmtemp_probe(), detect_work is registered for cancellation via
devm_delayed_work_autocancel(). During driver detach, devres_release_all()
first moves all existing entries from dev->devres_head onto a local todo
list before invoking their release callbacks in reverse order. If
create_dimm_temp_info_delayed() is already running when
devm_delayed_work_drop() calls cancel_delayed_work_sync(),
create_dimm_temp_info() can allocate dimmtemp_label strings via
devm_kzalloc()/devm_kasprintf() and register the hwmon device via
devm_hwmon_device_register_with_info(), appending new devres entries to
the now-empty dev->devres_head. Once the work finishes,
devres_release_all() frees priv and priv->name from the local todo list
without re-evaluating dev->devres_head, leaving the late devres
allocations and registered hwmon device behind with a dangling priv
pointer.

Cancel detect_work synchronously in a driver .remove() callback instead
of relying on devm_delayed_work_autocancel() so that the work is fully
drained before devres_release_all() detaches dev->devres_head, allowing
any devm resources registered by the delayed work to be released in
proper reverse order. Also only schedule detect_work when
check_populated_dimms() returns -EAGAIN so that probe failure paths do
not leave delayed work pending.
items.title: hwmon: (peci/dimmtemp) Fix devres leak and UAF on concurrent unbind

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

hwmon: (pmbus/q54sj108a2) Add missing NULL pointer check

When CONFIG_DEBUG_FS is enabled and per-client PMBus debugfs directory
creation fails during pmbus_do_probe(), q54sj108a2_probe() passes the NULL
pointer returned by pmbus_get_debugfs_dir() to debugfs_create_dir()
without validation, creating its debugfs directory at the debugfs root
instead of under the client directory.

If pmbus_init_debugfs() fails to create the client directory, data->debugfs
is left as NULL or an ERR_PTR, which pmbus_get_debugfs_dir() converts to
NULL. Passing a NULL parent to debugfs_create_dir() places q54sj108a2_dir
in the root of the debugfs filesystem and populates it with attribute files
whose private data pointers reference psu->debugfs_entries. Because this
root-level directory is outside the client debugfs hierarchy, PMBus core
cleanup does not remove it on device unbind, leaking the debugfs entries
and causing a use-after-free of the devm-allocated struct q54sj108a2_data
if the orphaned files are accessed via q54sj108a2_debugfs_read() or
q54sj108a2_debugfs_write() after device removal.

Fix the problem by adding the missing NULL pointer check.
items.title: hwmon: (pmbus/q54sj108a2) Add missing NULL pointer check

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

hwmon: (coretemp) Set nr_cores only after core_data allocation succeeds

In init_temp_data(), pdata->nr_cores is populated from
topology_num_cores_per_package() before allocating pdata->core_data. If
that allocation fails, init_temp_data() returns NULL with
pdata->core_data still NULL and pdata->nr_cores set to a positive value.

coretemp_add_core() logs the error without failing coretemp_cpu_online(),
so the CPU still comes online with pdata->hwmon_dev registered. When the
CPU is later taken offline (or the module is unloaded),
coretemp_cpu_offline() calls get_temp_data(pd, cpu), which loops up to
pdata->nr_cores and dereferences the NULL pdata->core_data pointer.

Store the core count in a local variable and assign pdata->nr_cores only
after pdata->core_data is allocated, preserving the invariant that
pdata->nr_cores is zero whenever pdata->core_data is NULL.
items.title: hwmon: (coretemp) Set nr_cores only after core_data allocation succeeds

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvme-rdma: fix NULL queue->ctrl dereference on reconnect

Since commit 2a8513091d2f ("nvme-rdma: parallelize I/O queue allocation
and startup"), a reconnect that gets more I/O queues than before grows
the tag set before the new queues are set up. queue->ctrl is only set
by nvme_rdma_setup_io_queues(), so I/O submitted in between reaches
nvme_rdma_queue_rq() on a queue that was never allocated and
dereferences a NULL queue->ctrl:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 000000000000034c
  RIP: 0010:nvme_rdma_queue_rq+0x52/0xb90

Set queue->ctrl for every queue when allocating the controller. Such
requests are then requeued like on any other queue that is not live.
items.title: nvme-rdma: fix NULL queue->ctrl dereference on reconnect

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvme: Do not drop the cdev reference twice when cdev_device_add() fails

Since commit 9952f3882ecb ("nvme: fix cdev lifetime"),
nvme_add_ns_cdev() and nvme_add_ns_head_cdev() take a reference to the
namespace (or namespace head) before calling nvme_cdev_add(), to be
dropped by the char device's release, nvme_cdev_rel(), and drop it
themselves when nvme_cdev_add() fails. But when cdev_device_add()
fails, nvme_cdev_add() has already put the device, and nvme_cdev_rel()
has already dropped that reference: the caller drops it a second time.

With one allocation failure injected into cdev_device_add() for a
namespace on an NVMe over loop controller, deleting the controller
gives, with native multipath:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in nvme_put_ns_head+0x21/0x140
  Write of size 4 at addr ff1100000a4ea078 by task init/1
   nvme_put_ns_head
   nvme_put_ns
   nvme_remove_namespaces
   nvme_do_delete_ctrl
   nvme_delete_ctrl_sync
   nvme_sysfs_delete
  Freed by task 1:
   kfree
   nvme_ns_remove
   nvme_remove_namespaces
  refcount_t: underflow; use-after-free.

Take the reference in nvme_cdev_add() instead, right before
cdev_device_add(), and let the callers neither take nor drop it. Add
nvme_is_ns_cdev() for the check that nvme_cdev_rel() and nvme_cdev_add()
now share.
items.title: nvme: Do not drop the cdev reference twice when cdev_device_add() fails

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86/mmu: Conditionally resched when retrying gPTE walk on A/D update failure

Conditionally reschedule when retrying a guest PTE walk because the CMPXCHG
to update A/D bits failed, e.g. because a different task/vCPU modified the
relevant gPTEs.  On kernels without involuntary preemption of some kind, a
misbehaving guest can "capture" a pCPU effectively indefinitely and trigger
soft lockups by continuously modifying its gPTEs such that the result of
the walk is remains valid.
items.title: KVM: x86/mmu: Conditionally resched when retrying gPTE walk on A/D update failure

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Conditionally resched when restarting REP string emulation

When restarting emulation, e.g. of a REP-prefixed string instruction,
conditionally reschedule as emulating guest writes can be deceptively slow
and expensive, e.g. when shadow paging is in use and each write can trigger
write tracking.

In a perfect world, restarting emulation (or not) would be less arbitrary,
e.g. would honor not only host events (NEED_RESCHED, signals, etc.) but
also guest events (e.g. by checking kvm_vcpu_has_events()).  Unfortunately,
as pointed out by Sashiko, pio_in_emulated()'s read-ahead logic is baked
into the restart logic, as KVM relies on restarting emulation to drain the
cache and avoid duplicate reads from the I/O port.  I.e. re-entering the
guest on kvm_vcpu_has_events() or __xfer_to_guest_mode_work_pending() would
introduce architecturally-incorrect, guest-visible changes.
items.title: KVM: x86: Conditionally resched when restarting REP string emulation

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv6: reject wrapped temporary address preferred lifetimes

ipv6_create_tempaddr() raises a temporary address's preferred lifetime to
regen_advance + age + 1 when the configured lifetime is too short. The
result is stored in a u32, while regen_advance and age are unsigned long.
If the sum wraps or is truncated, the stored lifetime can still be less
than or equal to regen_advance + age.

addrconf_verify_rtnl() then sees the new address as due for regeneration
and creates another one. Temporary addresses are not limited by
max_addresses since commit 4b08a8f1bd8c ("ipv6: remove max_addresses
check from ipv6_create_tempaddr"), so this can cause unbounded address
growth. With dad_transmits set to -1, a baseline kernel reached 2859
loopback addresses in two seconds.

After storing the adjusted lifetime, verify that it is still greater than
regen_advance + age. Reject the new address if the check fails.

On an x86-64 KASAN kernel, the normal configuration created three IPv6
addresses. The negative dad_transmits, positive multiplication overflow,
and large retransmission-time cases each left only the loopback and public
addresses. An i386 defconfig and an x86-64 allmodconfig both built
addrconf.o with W=1.
items.title: ipv6: reject wrapped temporary address preferred lifetimes

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/khugepaged: flush deferred unmaps before dropping a failed folio

collapse_file() can fail its reference-count or dirty-folio check after
unmapping with TTU_BATCH_FLUSH.  Both paths put back the isolated folio,
then unlock it and drop the lookup reference before reaching the common
try_to_unmap_flush().

The page-cache reference does not keep the folio stable once the lock is
released.  Another collapse can replace and free it.  With its PTEs
already gone, that collapse cannot flush the first task's per-task TLB
batch, and retract_page_tables() skips short or unaligned VMAs.  A CPU can
therefore retain a user translation to the freed folio.  This has been
reproduced with unprivileged MADV_COLLAPSE on a memfd.

Flush at out_unlock while the lookup reference and folio lock are still
held.  The common flush continues to cover the accumulated pagelist on
both success and rollback, preserving batching on successful collapses.
items.title: mm/khugepaged: flush deferred unmaps before dropping a failed folio

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm: fix address wraparound when scanning large folio PTEs

numa_rebuild_large_mapping() and do_swap_page() can be tricked into
generating an address wraparound, crashing the kernel. All that's required
is to map a tail page of a large folio close enough to the start/end of
the address space to e.g., make

	unsigned long addr_start = addr - (nr << PAGE_SHIFT);

to wrap around.

Let's fix it by providing a better helper, folio_scan_range(), that
takes care of staying within VMA and page table boundaries while
handling possible wraparounds.

There are some nasty details, like not being able to use pmd_addr_end()
in this context. Add some helpful comments for these cases.
items.title: mm: fix address wraparound when scanning large folio PTEs

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm: memory: fix truncation removing mapped folios

Ayush reported an issue that shmem/tmpfs folios are still mapped when
truncating them on production:
"
BUG: Bad page cache in process ...  pfn:...
page dumped because: still mapped when deleted
"

I reproduced the issue with Ayush's reproducer [1] with the latest
mm-unstable branch, and I got the following crash info.  From the dump
message, we can see that truncate_inode_folio() is really trying to remove
mapped folios, which is incorrect.

"
[  189.171977] page: refcount:3 mapcount:1 mapping:00000000fe168ee1
index:0x3880 pfn:0x191647
[  189.171995] memcg:ffff0000cc073d40
[  189.171997] aops:shmem_aops ino:3c01 dentry name(?):"memfd:runsc-memory"
[  189.172006] flags: 0x17fffef0002022d(locked|referenced|uptodate|lru|
workingset|swapbacked|node=0|zone=2|lastcpupid=0x3ffff)
.......
[  189.172017] page dumped because: VM_BUG_ON_FOLIO(folio_mapped(folio))
[  189.172026] ------------[ cut here ]------------
[  189.172027] kernel BUG at mm/filemap.c:155!
[  189.172057] Internal error: Oops - BUG: 00000000f2000800 [#1]  SMP
.......
[  189.177721] CPU: 3 UID: 0 PID: 5521 Comm: repro Kdump: loaded Tainted:
7.3.0-rc4+ #277 PREEMPT(lazy)
.......
[  189.183986] Call trace:
[  189.184124]  filemap_unaccount_folio+0xf0/0x1e8 (P)
[  189.184391]  __filemap_remove_folio+0x34/0x160
[  189.184633]  filemap_remove_folio+0x4c/0xb0
[  189.184859]  truncate_inode_folio+0x34/0x58
[  189.185087]  shmem_undo_range+0x220/0x658
[  189.185308]  shmem_fallocate+0x2f0/0x470
[  189.185527]  vfs_fallocate+0x128/0x328
......
[  189.187078]  el0t_64_sync+0x184/0x188
"

After analysis, I believe the race exists between truncation and
MADV_DONTNEED, and shmem's ->map_pages() merely makes the issue easier to
reproduce.  Since MADV_DONTNEED synchronously releases the pagetable page
before calling tlb_flush_rmaps(), this could cause another thread's
truncation to skip zap_pte_range() (due to pmd is none) but still observe
the folio's mapcount as non-zero.  A possible race scenario is as follows:

CPU 0                           CPU 1
shmem_fallocate                 madvise_dontneed_single_vma
  unmap_mapping_range            .......
  ......
  (filemap_map_pages() remap folios)
				  zap_pte_range
  truncate_inode_folio		    zap_empty_pte_table(pmd clear)
    unmap_mapping_folio
    ......
      zap_pmd_range (saw pmd none, skip)

  filemap_remove_folio
    BUG_ON(folio_mapped)
                                    tlb_flush_rmaps(remove rmaps)

To fix this issue, we should move the pmd clear operation (via
zap_empty_pte_table()) to after tlb_flush_rmaps() and use
sync_with_folio_pmd_zap() to sync with concurrent zapping, so that when we
find a pmd_none() while unmapping a folio without holding the PTL, the
folio's mappings are guaranteed to have been removed via
tlb_flush_rmaps().

Meanwhile move the second pmd_none() check to where it belongs: if
splitting zapped the PMD.
items.title: mm: memory: fix truncation removing mapped folios

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/page-writeback: avoid 32-bit overflow in dirty threshold shares

The ratios used by __wb_calc_thresh() are scaled to parts per million, but
the threshold and ratio operands are unsigned long.  On 32-bit kernels,
their multiplication can wrap before the result is assigned to u64.

For example, with a threshold of 25600 pages and the default maximum ratio
of 1000000, wb_max_thresh becomes 4125 pages instead of 25600.  The shared
threshold and minimum share calculations can overflow in the same way,
producing incorrect per-writeback dirty limits.

Use a u64 threshold for the three ratio multiplications and div_u64() to
retain the existing division order and rounding.
items.title: mm/page-writeback: avoid 32-bit overflow in dirty threshold shares

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/hugetlb: fix mremap deadlock when PMD sharing is possible

move_hugetlb_page_tables() holds the mapping's i_mmap_rwsem for
write while moving hugetlb PTEs. This prevents races with truncation
and protects huge_pmd_unshare(), but the move loop must not call
helpers that can acquire the same rwsem for read.

huge_pte_alloc() can do that when the destination can use PMD
sharing: it may call huge_pmd_share(), which takes i_mmap_rwsem for
read while searching for a shareable PMD table. Calling it while the
move path already holds i_mmap_rwsem for write can deadlock.

Avoid that path for PMD-sized hugetlb mappings that can use PMD
sharing. Instead of allocating or sharing the destination page table
while moving, zap the source range and let the destination fault path
populate or share the PMD lazily.

Reuse the hugetlb unmap logic for the source-side zap by splitting
the core loop out of __unmap_hugepage_range(). The wrapper keeps the
existing tlb_start_vma(), tlb_end_vma() and huge_pmd_unshare_flush()
behavior, while move_hugetlb_page_tables() can reuse the unmap loop
with its existing mmu_gather.
items.title: mm/hugetlb: fix mremap deadlock when PMD sharing is possible

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/vma: write lock source VMA before duplicating it in __split_vma()

__split_vma() duplicates the source VMA before taking its VMA write lock,
and until the VMA is write-locked, a concurrent thread might set
VMA_MAYBE_GUARD_BIT, resulting in the duplication missing the flag.

If this happens, then fork may fail to duplicate guard markers and, if a
file-backed mapping, THP collapse may also discard the markers.

Resolve this by taking the VMA write lock before vm_area_dup() and, since
all callers of vm_area_dup() now hold the VMA write lock, assert that this
is the case there, and add a comment to explain why it's needed.

[ljs@kernel.org: add VMA write assert in vm_area_dup(), commit message touchup]
items.title: mm/vma: write lock source VMA before duplicating it in __split_vma()

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/ksm: fix userfaultfd protection during merge and unmerge

KSM loses userfaultfd protection when replace_page() builds a new PTE from
vma->vm_page_prot.  Dropping its uffd bit lets a subsequent write go
through ordinary COW instead of userfaultfd write protection handling. 
For RWP, a merged page also becomes readable without faulting.

Keeping the uffd bit and restoring PAGE_NONE fixes merging, but we also
have to handle unmerging.  An existing KSM page can be protected with RWP
before MADV_UNMERGEABLE, so unmerging already needs fixing independently
of preserving RWP during merging.

Unsharing replaces a shared page with a private one and should leave
userfaultfd protection in place, as do_wp_page() already does for write
protection.  Currently, an unshare fault reaches do_uffd_rwp() before it
can proceed to do_wp_page().

- With synchronous RWP, handle_userfault() returns VM_FAULT_SIGBUS.
  break_ksm() then reports success with a KSM page still merged.

- With asynchronous RWP, protection is cleared before unsharing.

Preserve the uffd bit when merging, and restore PAGE_NONE for RWP.  Let
FAULT_FLAG_UNSHARE skip RWP fault handling and keep PAGE_NONE on each
private copy as well.  Unsharing can then complete with RWP still armed
for a subsequent access.
items.title: mm/ksm: fix userfaultfd protection during merge and unmerge

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/hugetlb_vmemmap: map the shared tail page writable

page_ref_add_unless_zero() reads the refcount and then updates it with a
cmpxchg.  A lockless get, such as a page cache lookup or a PFN scanner,
can read a non-zero refcount from a page that is then freed and reused as
a hugetlb tail page.  If HVO remaps its struct page to the shared tail
page in between, the cmpxchg writes to read-only vmemmap:

    CPU0 (lockless get)               CPU1
    c = atomic_read(&page->_refcount)
                                      page freed
                                      page allocated as a hugetlb tail
                                      HVO remaps the struct page RO
    try_cmpxchg(&page->_refcount, &c, c + 1)
      -> write fault on read-only vmemmap

The refcount is zero by then and the compare fails, but a compare-and-swap
instruction needs write access whether or not it succeeds.  The kernel
oopses when hugetlb pages are allocated at runtime with HVO enabled while
a lockless get races with it.

Commit bd225530a4c7 ("mm/hugetlb_vmemmap: fix race with speculative PFN
walkers") closed the window with RCU on both sides.  The RCU was removed
together with fake heads, on the wrong belief that it was only needed for
them.

Map the shared tail page writable instead of restoring the RCU.  Every
struct page on it is a tail with a zero refcount, so a late cmpxchg
fails and leaves the page unchanged.  RCU would put rcu_read_lock()
back around every get and synchronize_rcu() back into hugetlb
allocation and freeing.

The cost is the protection against stray writes to tail struct pages.  The
shared page is shared by all hugetlb folios of the same order in the zone,
so such a write now corrupts all of them instead of oopsing.

Bootmem folios optimized when the memmap is set up keep their tails
read-only.  Nothing does a lockless get on them before hugetlb takes them
over.
items.title: mm/hugetlb_vmemmap: map the shared tail page writable

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/cma: accept memory of multi-range CMA areas

Patch series "mm/cma: accept memory of CMA areas reserved with
memblock_reserve()", v1.

Pages of allocated CMA areas are released to the buddy allocator with
__free_pages(), which does not check for unaccepted memory.

This usually works because memblock accepts the memory it allocates.

However, multi-range CMA areas, used by hugetlb_cma, and fixed CMA areas
requested with cma=<size>@<base> are reserved with memblock_reserve() and
their memory is never accepted.

On TDX and SEV-SNP guests the first access to such a page is fatal.

To ease the backporting, each case is addressed by a separate patch:
- patch 1 accepts the memory of multi-range CMA areas
- patch 2 does the same for the fixed CMA areas

The second patch won't apply cleanly to 6.6 and 6.12, but I believe the
stable team LLMs will take care of that :)


This patch (of 2):

On systems with unaccepted memory, memblock allocations accept the
allocated range, but when cma_declare_contiguous_multi() uses open coded
allocation of multiple ranges, it reserves them with memblock_reserve()
and they are never accepted.

These pages are released to the buddy allocator by cma_activate_area()
with __free_pages() that does not check for unaccepted memory, so the
first access to such a page in a TDX or SEV-SNP guest is fatal.

Accept the memory of each range when it is reserved.
items.title: mm/cma: accept memory of multi-range CMA areas

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/cma: accept memory of CMA areas reserved at a fixed address

CMA areas allocated from memblock have their memory accepted by
memblock_alloc_range_nid(), but areas reserved at a fixed address with
memblock_reserve() are not.

If a fixed CMA area is requested by the cma=<size>@<base> command line
parameter, it may be in regular RAM and on TDX and SEV-SNP guests it
must be accepted.

Accept the memory of fixed CMA areas as well, so that all CMA areas are
accepted regardless of how they were reserved.
items.title: mm/cma: accept memory of CMA areas reserved at a fixed address

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm: memcontrol: fix NULL pointer deref and UAF from high_work_func() on dying memcg

When memory.high is exceeded in non-task context, try_charge_memcg()
schedules memcg->high_work without taking a reference on the memcg, and
high_work_func() invokes reclaim_high() without pinning the memcg.

With obj_cgroup reparenting, introduced in commit bf4f059954dc ("mm:
memcg/slab: obj_cgroup API"), objects charged to a child memcg are
reparented to its parent in mem_cgroup_css_offline() instead of holding a
reference on the child until uncharged.  Subsequent uncharges of those
objects go to the parent, which can leave the child's memory use
permanently above its high limit, so any later charge on the offlined
memcg in non-task context schedules high_work.  This was later widened
from kernel memory to LRU folios when commit f1cf8d2f36dc ("mm:
memcontrol: eliminate the problem of dying memory cgroup for LRU folios")
converted LRU folios to use obj_cgroup reparenting.

cancel_work_sync(&memcg->high_work) only runs at the end of teardown in
mem_cgroup_css_free(), so high_work_func() can start or still be running
reclaim_high() after mem_cgroup_css_released() or shrink_many() has called
lru_gen_release_memcg() and unhashed lruvec->lrugen.list.  If reclaim
tries to rotate the memcg, lru_gen_rotate_memcg() dereferences a NULL
pprev pointer.  This issue is specific to MGLRU and was introduced with
the memcg LRU in commit e4dde56cd208 ("mm: multi-gen LRU: per-node
lru_gen_folio lists").

With either traditional LRU or MGLRU, css_free_rwork_fn() calls
css_rstat_exit() which frees per-CPU rstat data before calling
mem_cgroup_css_free().  If reclaim_high() is still running, rstat updates
via mod_lruvec_state() -> __css_rstat_updated() cause a use-after-free on
the per-CPU rstat data.  This was introduced when commit 5da3bfa029d6
("cgroup: use separate rstat trees for each subsystem") moved
css_rstat_exit() ahead of ss->css_free().

Fix both problems by acquiring a reference with css_tryget_online() in
high_work_func() before calling reclaim_high(), and by resetting
memory.high and swap.high to PAGE_COUNTER_MAX in mem_cgroup_css_offline()
so that charges via references on an offlined memcg do not trigger
high_work on the dead child and skip checking live ancestors in
try_charge_memcg().

Acquiring the reference in high_work_func() rather than before scheduling
high_work is safe because mem_cgroup_css_free() calls irq_work_sync() and
cancel_work_sync() which cancels pending work and waits for an already
running high_work_func() to complete before mem_cgroup_free() frees the
memcg.  css_tryget_online() uses percpu_ref_tryget_live() and is safe to
call after percpu_ref_exit() before the cgroup is freed unlike
css_tryget().

Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc0000000000: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000000-0x0000000000000007]
CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 27 Comm: kworker/1:0 Tainted: G    B   W           7.3.0-rc5-g2bba28e98578 #284 PREEMPT(full)
Tainted: [B]=BAD_PAGE, [W]=WARN  <-- Taint from lru_gen_rotate_memcg() VM_WARN_ON_ONCE
Hardware name: QEMU Standard PC (i440FX + PIIX, 1996), BIOS 1.17.0-debian-1.17.0-1 04/01/2014
Workqueue: events high_work_func
RIP: 0010:lru_gen_rotate_memcg+0x1a3/0xe90
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 ? read_ctrl_pos+0x22f/0x3f0
 shrink_lruvec+0x16cb/0x1b80
 ? ret_from_fork_asm+0x1a/0x30
 ? lapic_next_event+0x15/0x20
 ? clockevents_program_event+0x2bb/0x6f0
 ? lapic_next_event+0x15/0x20
 ? __pfx_shrink_lruvec+0x10/0x10
 ? __pfx_clockevents_program_event+0x10/0x10
 ? _raw_spin_lock+0x84/0xe0

 ? kasan_save_stack+0x30/0x50
 ? psi_group_change+0x381/0x740
 ? __pfx_sched_clock_cpu+0x10/0x10

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: find the xattr entry again after defragmenting a bucket

ocfs2_xattr_set_entry_bucket() hands loc.xl_entry to ocfs2_xa_set() twice:
once for the bucket as it stands, and, if that reports -ENOSPC, once more
after ocfs2_defrag_xattr_bucket() has packed the name/value pairs down.

Defragmenting ends by sorting the entry array on xe_name_hash.  Buckets
are kept sorted, so the sort only permutes entries that share a hash, but
lib/sort.c is an unstable heapsort and it does permute them.  loc.xl_entry
is an address inside xh_entries[], so afterwards it denotes whichever
entry landed in that slot rather than the one the search found.

The second ocfs2_xa_set() then works on the wrong entry.  Nothing on that
path compares the entry's name with xi->xi_name, so what happens depends
on how the two entries compare in size: ocfs2_xa_reuse_entry() trips its
BUG_ON() when the padded name sizes differ, and otherwise the new value is
written into the neighbouring attribute's value slot while the attribute
being set is left untouched.  setxattr() reports success either way.

Remember the entry's hash before defragmenting and look the entry up
again afterwards, the way ocfs2_xattr_bucket_find() does.  An entry that
cannot be found again means the bucket no longer holds what the search
found, so fail with -EFSCORRUPTED rather than writing through the stale
pointer.
items.title: ocfs2: find the xattr entry again after defragmenting a bucket

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: find the xattr entry again after converting a block to a bucket

ocfs2_xattr_create_index_block() turns a non-indexed xattr block into a
tree by copying it into a bucket, and the copy sorts the entries: a
block holds them in insertion order, a bucket by name hash.
ocfs2_xattr_update_xattr_search() nevertheless relocates the caller's
search by the index the entry had in the block, so unless the two orders
agreed it points at an unrelated entry, and nothing between there and
the write compares that entry's name with the one being set.

Setting an xattr whose new value no longer fits the block arrives here
with xs->not_found clear.  The block gave up because
ocfs2_xa_block_can_reuse() wants an exact namevalue size match, while
ocfs2_xa_bucket_can_reuse() only wants an entry at least as large as the
new one, so the bucket accepts a pair the block rejected and the update
lands on whichever entry the sort left at that index.  Equal padded name
lengths get that other attribute's value replaced in place and its name
left alone, so setxattr returns success while the attribute asked for
keeps its old value.  A longer one trips ocfs2_xa_reuse_entry()'s
BUG_ON, and a shorter one is refused by the bucket as well, so
ocfs2_xa_prepare_entry() wipes the entry and writes the new name over
it, leaving xe_name_hash describing a name that is no longer there.

Find the entry again by the name being set, matching the type as well.
The copy carries every entry and every name over unchanged, and (type,
name) pairs are unique within a block, so the match is exact.  The type
matters because the handlers strip their prefix before calling
ocfs2_xattr_set(), so user.foo and trusted.foo share a stored name, a
stored length and a hash, and both can sit in the same block.

The name has to come from xi rather than from xs->here: a failed set can
remove the entry xs->here names, and only the "growing" caller sets
ctxt->set_abort, which is what stops the conversion.  Scan every entry
rather than narrowing on the hash the way ocfs2_find_xe_in_bucket()
does, since an existing entry keeps the hash it was stored under, which
a kernel that sign-extended the name bytes made different from the one
computed now.  An empty result means the entry did not survive the
failed set and this has become an insert; leaving xs->here alone would
keep it pointing into the block, which is rewritten as a tree root
before the caller reads it again.
items.title: ocfs2: find the xattr entry again after converting a block to a bucket

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: do not index before the entry array when dividing an empty bucket

ocfs2_divide_xattr_bucket() appends an empty bucket carrying a sentinel
hash when the source bucket has no divide position, taking that hash
from xh_entries[start - 1].  ocfs2_xattr_find_divide_pos() returns count
when every entry shares one hash, and its loop does not run at all for
count < 2, so an empty bucket comes back with start == count == 0 and
the read is xh_entries[-1].

That is outside the __counted_by_le(xh_count) bounds of xh_entries[] and
lands on the header, so the value picked up is
xh_count | xh_free_start << 16.  One above it is written into the new
bucket's xh_entries[0] and committed, which leaves a bucket whose first
hash does not follow the bucket before it.  ocfs2_xattr_bucket_find()
binary searches on xh_entries[0], so the broken key hides the range the
sentinel was meant to cover: getxattr() answers -ENODATA for an
attribute that is stored, and an insert can go to the wrong bucket and
leave two copies of a name.  The cross cluster divide hands the same
value back as a tree record's e_cpos, which then claims a hash range it
does not cover.

Read xh_entries[0] instead.  The branch is only reached when every entry
shares one hash, so for a non-empty bucket it holds the same value, and
for an empty one it is the slot that carries the bucket key.

An empty bucket reaches the divide from
ocfs2_check_xattr_bucket_collision(), which reports no collision for
one, through ocfs2_add_new_xattr_bucket() and
ocfs2_extend_xattr_bucket().  It does not take a failed set to get
there: a divide that finds no position is itself what leaves an empty
sentinel bucket behind, and a later extend can pick it as the target.
items.title: ocfs2: do not index before the entry array when dividing an empty bucket

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2/dlm: serialize migration MLE cleanup on failure

A migration MLE has a base reference for the mastering answer and an
in-use reference held by dlm_migrate_lockres(). The finishing assertion
consumes the base reference, but migration failure drops it again
without checking whether the assertion already consumed it.

The target queues its migration worker before it acknowledges the
ALL_DONE packet, so its finishing assertion can be handled while the
sender still waits for the status. If the connection fails before the
status arrives, dlm_send_one_lockres() returns an error for a migration
that the target has already completed:

  Old-master sender                  Finishing assertion
  -----------------                  -------------------
  publish MLE; take in-use reference
  send ALL_DONE; wait for status
                                     take lookup reference
                                     unlink MLE
                                     put lookup and base references
  send returns a connection error
  put base reference again; free MLE
  put in-use reference; access freed MLE

dlm_assert_master_handler() holds dlm->spinlock from the MLE lookup to
the final puts, and it takes dlm->master_lock around the unlink and the
puts. Decide under the same locks: if the MLE is already unhashed, the
assertion consumed the base reference, so drop only the sender's in-use
reference. Otherwise unlink it before consuming the base reference so a
later assertion no longer finds it.

An assertion that got there first has also made the target the owner
and cleared DLM_LOCK_RES_MIGRATING. Treating the attempt as failed at
that point would leave the lockres owned by the target while this node
still holds the other nodes' locks and refmap bits, so it could neither
be purged nor migrated again. Finish our side as a completed migration
does instead: drop those locks under res->spinlock if the target still
owns the lockres, and recalculate its usage.

Use the same cleanup for the pre-send failure, the send failure and the
target-death failure paths. The sender's in-use reference keeps the MLE
alive until its final put outside the nested locks. Successful
migration retains its existing in-use-only put.

A target that has died cannot assert after the sender has seen its
death. The o2net node-down callback runs before the DLM one; it
disconnects the node and flushes the workqueue that runs the message
handlers, so an assertion already received has been handled by the time
the DLM removes the node from the domain map. A node that leaves the
domain cleanly sends its exit message only after its assertions have
been answered.

Two windows of the hand-over itself are left as they are: the handler
switches the owner and the sender drops the other nodes' locks moments
later, and an assertion from a live target that arrives after the
sender has given up still meets the owner check in the handler. Waiting
for the target before giving up would only stretch the first window
into the time in which recovery of the target can observe it.

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: stop recovery before shutting down local allocators

Recovery completion needs the local allocators until it has finished
reclaiming a failed node's allocation window and truncate log.  During
unmount, quota recovery is stopped first, but that leaves recovery_state
at OCFS2_REC_QUOTA_DISABLED.  New non-quota recovery can still start.

ocfs2_truncate_log_shutdown() drains existing completion work and releases
osb_tl_bh before ocfs2_recovery_exit() closes that publication path:

  Unmount                             Recovery
  -------                             --------
  stop quota recovery; disable quotas
  truncate_log_shutdown()
    flush existing completion work
                                      recover another failed node
                                        queue completion
    flush local log; release buffer
                                      complete_truncate_log_recovery()
                                        use released osb_tl_bh
  recovery_exit(): disable and drain

An extra buffer reference alone would still let completion append new
records after the final truncate-log flush.

Split stopping and draining recovery from freeing its state. Stop all
recovery producers and drain completion work before shutting down either
local allocator. Keep recovery-state release at its existing later point,
so its lifetime relative to other teardown users stays unchanged. The
second stop at recovery_exit() is harmless once recovery is disabled.

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2/cluster: unlink socket containers before releasing resources

A socket container's node and socket must remain alive while the
container is on sock_containers. The debugfs formatter reads sc_node
and sc_sock under o2net_debug_lock without taking their references, but
sc_kref_release() releases both before taking that lock to unlink the
container.

With CONFIG_DEBUG_FS enabled, a synchronous sender can retain its last
socket-container reference after o2net_disconnect_node() has detached
the connection and flushed o2net_wq. The caller runs outside that
workqueue. After the sender removes its configfs dependency, node
removal can proceed without waiting for the sender's final sc_put():

  Sender (final sc_put)    Configfs rmdir        Debugfs reader
  --------------------    --------------        --------------
  o2nm_undepend_item()
                          Drop node item refs
  o2nm_node_put()
    [node can be freed]
                                               sc_seq_show()
                                                 Lock debug lock
                                                 Read sc_node->nd_name
                                                 Unlock debug lock
  sc_node = NULL
  o2net_debug_del_sc()

The earlier socket release has a similar window. The container is
still selectable while its socket has been released and sc_sock has
not yet been cleared:

  Sender (final sc_put)                       Debugfs reader
  --------------------                       --------------
  sock_release(sc->sc_sock)
    [socket can be freed]
                                             sc_seq_show()
                                               Lock debug lock
                                               Read sc_sock->sk fields
                                               Unlock debug lock
  sc_sock = NULL
  ...
  o2net_debug_del_sc()

Move o2net_debug_del_sc() before releasing either resource. Unlinking
under the existing debug lock waits for an active formatter to finish
and prevents later readers from selecting the container. This covers
both socket fields and node fields, including nd_num in the stats
formatter.
